name: django-blog-admin
title: Pergament - Django long-form blog with admin backoffice
description: A server-rendered publishing blog (Markdown posts, categories, moderated comments, RSS, search) using classic Django session auth and the built-in Django admin as its CMS-style backoffice.
build: .venv/bin/python manage.py migrate --noinput && .venv/bin/python manage.py collectstatic --noinput && .venv/bin/python manage.py seed_demo

env.name: DJANGO_SECRET_KEY
env.description: Django SECRET_KEY used for sessions/CSRF signing. Set a long random value in production.

env.name: DJANGO_DEBUG
env.description: 1/true enables Django debug mode (never in production).

env.name: DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS
env.description: Comma-separated list of allowed Host header values.

env.name: DJANGO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS
env.description: Comma-separated origins WITH scheme (e.g. https://blog.example.com); required for form POSTs when served over HTTPS behind a proxy.

env.name: DJANGO_DB_PATH
env.description: SQLite file path; absolute or relative to the project root. Parent directory is created automatically. The Docker image sets /app/data/db.sqlite3.

auth.description: Django contrib.auth session cookies (sessionid + csrftoken). /accounts/login/ POSTs a CSRF-protected form; /write/, /dashboard/ and post editing require a logged-in user; /admin/ requires is_staff. Logout is POST-only.

persistence: SQLite file at data/db.sqlite3 (DJANGO_DB_PATH); Docker image stores it at /app/data (declared VOLUME). Created by `migrate`, seeded idempotently by `seed_demo` (entrypoint.sh runs both on every start).
notes: Single container, no external services. entrypoint.sh runs migrate -> collectstatic -> seed_demo -> gunicorn on $PORT (8003). Mount a writable volume at /app/data to keep posts across restarts. When served over HTTPS via a reverse proxy set DJANGO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS to the public origin, otherwise login/comment form POSTs fail CSRF checks. Static files are served by WhiteNoise from the same process (no separate static server needed). Requires Python 3.12+ locally (verified on 3.14; Docker image uses 3.12).
